scenario.context: QuickRead is a news app. The team wants to grow engaged readership without annoying users.

steps.task: Define a north-star metric, 2 input metrics, 2 guardrails and 1 counter-metric, each with a clear definition.
hints: The north star should reflect value to the reader, not just opens.
Guardrails protect experience, counter-metrics catch gaming.

content.northStar: Weekly engaged readers — users who read at least 3 articles (each for 30 seconds or more) in a week.

inputs.name: Articles read per session
inputs.definition: Average articles read to the end (or 30 seconds+) per session.

inputs.name: Sessions per week per active user

reference.whyItWorks: Measures real reading, names the levers, and watches for harm and gaming.
commonMistakes: Using app opens or downloads as the north star

scenario.context: A food-delivery app is launching scheduled orders, where customers pick a delivery slot up to 3 days ahead. Operations worry it may hurt instant-order delivery times.

steps.task: Define success metrics for the launch: a north star, 2 input metrics, 3 guardrails, and counter-metrics, with definitions and reasons.
hints: Success needs both adoption and reliability.
Think about what scheduled orders could harm on the supply side.

content.northStar: Scheduled orders delivered within the promised 15-minute window per week.

inputs.name: Adoption
inputs.definition: % of active customers who place a scheduled order in a week.

guardrails.name: p90 delivery time for instant orders
Restaurant acceptance rate for scheduled orders

counter.name: Refunds per 1,000 scheduled orders
counter.definition: A reliable-looking number can hide customers who gave up.

reference.whyItWorks: Connects the customer promise to operational health on both sides.
commonMistakes: Ignoring the effect on the existing product
rubric: North star tied to the promise

scenario.context: WriteWell is an AI writing assistant that suggests sentences while users write. Usage is high, but the team is unsure whether suggestions actually help, and inference costs are rising.

steps.task: Propose a metric set that measures value and quality rather than just usage, and explain how each metric could be gamed.
hints: Acceptance rate alone can be misleading.

content.northStar: Documents completed with at least one accepted suggestion and kept for 24 hours, per weekly active writer.

inputs.name: Documents started per weekly active writer

guardrails.name: Post-acceptance edit rate
guardrails.definition: Heavy edits mean the suggestion was poor.

counter.name: Share of users who accept more than 90% of suggestions with no edits

content.gaming: Gaming risks: showing fewer, easier suggestions inflates acceptance rate; autocompleting filler text inflates accepted words; both are caught by edit rate and kept-for-24-hours.

reference.whyItWorks: Measures outcomes and quality, accounts for cost, and anticipates Goodhart-style gaming.
commonMistakes: Using total suggestions shown or words generated as success
